title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: schema recommendations for custom connectors in the admin centre
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the recommendations, the navigation path, the schema-update API and the product-level licensing. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap's plans from the documented four-label checks and reports Microsoft's differing administrator-role guidance.

claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): [Copilot Extensibility] Schema Recommendations for Custom Connectors in M365 Admin Center

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Schema recommendations are accessed through the connection detail panel.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connection reaches the connection panel used to view recommendations.
claims.quote:
Go to **Copilot** > **Connectors** > **Your Connections**.
Select the connection that you want to modify.
Schema recommendations can be accessed via the connection detail panel.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The connector-management documentation requires an AI administrator to access and manage connectors.
claims.quote: To access and manage your Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator for your organization.

claims.claim: The Graph connection guide instead says a search admin can view and manage all tenant connections.
claims.quote: A search admin can view and manage all the connections in the tenant via the **Copilot** > **Agents and connectors** section of the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: An API for reading schema recommendations for a published custom connector is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: custom Copilot connectors schema recommendations API Microsoft Graph read disable default rollout licensing; "schema recommendations" "API" "disable". Opened manage-connector and Graph connectors API overview; neither documents a recommendations-read operation.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for updating the schema of the published custom connection to add missing labels.
claims.quote: Searched: custom connector schema semantic labels edit Microsoft 365 admin center Assign property labels SDK published connection. Opened manage-connector, manage-search-schema and SDK sample publish: update UI covers Microsoft-built connectors; SDK labels UI is during initial publishing.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/external/connections/{id}/schema creates or updates a connection schema.
claims.quote:
Create a new or update an existing schema for a Microsoft Search connection.
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr/schema

claims.claim: The schema-update request sets semantic labels through properties[].labels.
claims.quote:
"properties": [
    {
      "name": "ticketTitle",
      "type": "String",
      "isSearchable": "true",
      "isRetrievable": "true",
      "labels": [
        "title"
      ]

claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is the least privileged permission for schema updates.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All |
| Application | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All |

claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All is the higher privileged alternative for schema updates.
claims.quote:
| Permission type | Least privileged permissions | Higher privileged permissions |
| Application | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All |
